newsitem.title: UK: EMI slips on music slowdown worries.
newsitem.headline: EMI slips on music slowdown worries.

text.p: Shares in music company EMI slipped on Friday amid worries that years of strong growth in the industry may be coming to an end, traders said.
A report from the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry said worldwide sales were only marginally up in the first half of 1996 and real terms actually fell.
EMI shares fell in early trading, dropping to 1270p shortly after the start before paring losses to 1282-1/2p, an 18-1/2p fall.
But Nikko Securities analyst Dennis Exton said the report was not particularly new and the share price reaction overdone.
"It does remain to be seen about the second half. I think it will be better than the first but not neccessarily than the second half of last year," said Exton.

But EMI was best placed of the major five music groups because of the quality and extent of its music publishing business with many new outlets in the UK and abroad ranging from cable and satellite TV and commercial radio to the internet, he added.
"It is a very healthy,incremental revenue stream and insulates them from the worst."
